# Introduction

Proteomics missingness can be approximately intensity-independent (MAR-like)
or associated with low abundance and detection limits (MNAR-like). Features can
also be observed throughout one condition and absent throughout another.
Pooling samples can hide this on/off pattern.

ImputeFinder classifies unnormalised log2 protein intensities by condition and
filters unsupported features. Results record states, cutoffs, rescue values,
and drop reasons. **Likely MAR** and **likely MNAR** describe intensity-cutoff
classifications, not proven causes of missingness. The package neither
normalises nor imputes data.

Packages such as
[`DEP`][dep-guide],
[`MSnbase`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/MSnbase), and
[`msImpute`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/msImpute) provide broader analysis
or imputation workflows. ImputeFinder instead returns a matrix or
`SummarizedExperiment` with condition-specific groups for downstream treatment.
MNAR blocks can enter a detection-limit branch, MAR blocks a relationship-based
branch, and complete blocks pass through unchanged. The
[method comparison](#state-of-the-art-comparison) distinguishes these roles.

# Installation

Install the development package from GitHub. It requires R 4.6 or later and a
compatible Bioconductor library.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install("eturkes/imputefinder")

library(imputefinder)
```

Run the installed example from a writable folder:

```{r first-result, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "quickstart.R", package = "imputefinder",
    mustWork = TRUE))
```

It saves a labelled classification figure, result tables, and rescue records
under `imputefinder-results/`, replacing previous example files. Seven synthetic
features demonstrate retention and exclusion with manual cutoffs.

# Inputs and classification rules

Use an ordinary numeric matrix or a selected numeric `SummarizedExperiment`
assay. Rows hold named features, such as proteins, peptides, or PTM sites;
columns hold uniquely named samples. Align one condition label per sample.
Use `NA` for missing values; `NaN` and infinities are rejected. Zero stays
observed. ImputeFinder neither detects nor applies log transformation,
normalisation, centring, or scaling.

The worked examples use the legacy `rescue = "minimum"` policy. Each
feature-condition block receives exactly one state after that policy:

- `complete` - no value is missing.
- `MNAR` - at least one value is missing and the arithmetic mean of observed
    values is below the condition cutoff.
- `MAR` - at least one value is missing, the mean is at or above the cutoff,
    and strictly more than half the samples are observed.
- `insufficient` - the block is on the MAR side of the cutoff but lacks a
    strict observed majority.

With `rescue = "none"`, fully missing blocks instead receive `absent`.
They have no mean or assigned missingness mechanism and do not enter intensity
fitting. Other blocks follow the same rules. No missing values are replaced.

The arithmetic mean lets one strong observation move a partial block toward
MAR. Equality with the cutoff also falls on the MAR side. The strict-majority
rule provides minimum within-condition evidence for MAR candidates only. A
sparse low-intensity block can remain MNAR with one observation.

A feature is dropped when globally absent, `insufficient` in any condition, or
`MNAR` or `absent` in every condition. Otherwise it is retained, including
mixed states such as MNAR in one condition and complete in another.

```{r classification-workflow, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.7, fig.cap=workflow_caption}
workflow_nodes <- data.frame(
    x = c(0, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2),
    y = c(3, 3, 3, 1.9, 1.9, 1.9, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
    scope = c(rep("package", 6L), rep("external", 3L)),
    label = c(
        "Unnormalised log2\nmatrix + conditions",
        "Drop globally absent\nAnchor fully absent blocks",
        "Profile each condition\nChoose its intensity cutoff",
        "Classify each block\ncomplete / MAR / MNAR\n/ insufficient",
        "Drop whole features\nAny insufficient or\nall conditions MNAR",
        "Return filtered data\nStates + rescue log",
        "Normalise the\nreturned matrix",
        "Split by condition\nUse recorded labels",
        "Impute within condition\nRestore sample order"
    )
)
workflow_edges <- data.frame(
    x = c(0.43, 1.43, 2, 1.57, 0.57, 0, 0.43, 1.43),
    xend = c(0.57, 1.57, 2, 1.43, 0.43, 0, 0.57, 1.57),

)
ggplot2::ggplot() +

        fill = NA, colour = "#8297A5", linetype = "dashed") +
```

# Controlled example: mixed missingness across conditions

This synthetic panel combines low-intensity missingness, higher-intensity
missingness, and condition-specific absence. Four control and four treated
samples contain unnormalised log2-like intensities; both manual cutoffs are 12.
The panel explains classification and routing, not a biological experiment.

```{r manual-fixture}
x <- rbind(
    condition_on_off = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 16, 17, 16, 18),
    differential_mar = c(14, 15, NA, 16, 20, NA, 21, 22),
    mixed_mechanism = c(8, NA, NA, NA, 15, 16, NA, 17),
    high_tail_mar = c(8, 9, 25, NA, 14, 15, 16, 17),
    sparse_high = c(18, NA, NA, NA, 19, 20, 21, 22),
    all_mnar = c(7.5, NA, NA, NA, 8, NA, NA, NA),
    globally_absent = rep(NA_real_, 8),
    complete_low = c(8, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9),
    complete_high = c(18, 19, 18, 20, 20, 21, 22, 23)
)
sample_metadata <- data.frame(
    sample = c(paste0("control_", 1:4), paste0("treated_", 1:4)),
    condition = rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 4),
    replicate = rep(1:4, times = 2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
colnames(x) <- sample_metadata$sample
condition <- sample_metadata$condition

fit <- classify_missingness(
    x,
    group = condition,
    cutoffs = c(control = 12, treated = 12),
    seed = 1L
)
fit
```

```{r manual-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap=manual_heatmap_caption}
manual_heatmap <- data.frame(
    feature = rep(rownames(x), times = ncol(x)),
    sample = rep(colnames(x), each = nrow(x)),
    intensity = as.vector(x),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
manual_heatmap$feature <- factor(
    manual_heatmap$feature,
    levels = rev(rownames(x))
)
manual_heatmap$sample <- factor(
    manual_heatmap$sample,
    levels = colnames(x)
)
manual_heatmap$condition <- factor(
    sample_metadata$condition[
        match(as.character(manual_heatmap$sample), sample_metadata$sample)
    ],
    levels = c("control", "treated"),
    labels = c("Control", "Treated")
)
heatmap_sample_labels <- setNames(
    c(paste0("C", 1:4), paste0("T", 1:4)),
    colnames(x)
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    manual_heatmap,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature, fill = intensity)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = manual_heatmap[is.na(manual_heatmap$intensity), , drop = FALSE],
        mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 4,
        size = 2.1,
        stroke = 0.7,
        colour = "#555555"
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(
        cols = ggplot2::vars(condition),
        scales = "free_x",
        space = "free_x"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = heatmap_sample_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#F7FBFF",
        high = "#08519C",
        na.value = "#E0E0E0",
        name = "log2-like intensity"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Sample", y = "Synthetic protein") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
        legend.position = "right"
    )
```

Globally missing features are marked `all_missing` and removed. Each remaining
fully missing condition block receives one artificial anchor:

1. The minimum finite intensity in each condition is calculated before any
    anchors are inserted.
2. One sample in each fully missing feature-condition block is selected
    uniformly. Selection is with replacement across features.
3. Exactly that cell receives the condition minimum; the others remain `NA`.
4. The feature, condition, selected sample, old and inserted values, and seed
    are recorded.

```{r rescue-log}
fit$seed_log
fit$data["condition_on_off", ]
```

The anchor enables classification, not complete imputation. Original
observations stay unchanged. Stable name order and a local RNG scope make
rescue reproducible without changing the global RNG state.

`feature_status` covers every original feature, including dropped rows. The
classification table records evidence for each surviving feature-condition
state.

```{r classification-details}
fit$feature_status
fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$feature %in% c(
        "condition_on_off",
        "mixed_mechanism",
        "high_tail_mar",
        "sparse_high",
        "all_mnar"
    ),
    c("feature", "condition", "observed_count", "missing_count",
        "mean_intensity", "cutoff", "state", "retained", "drop_reason")
]
```

```{r manual-state-map, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5.1, fig.cap=manual_state_caption}
state_features <- setdiff(rownames(x), "globally_absent")
state_plot <- fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$feature %in% state_features,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
state_plot$feature <- factor(
    state_plot$feature,
    levels = rev(state_features)
)
state_plot$condition <- factor(
    state_plot$condition,
    levels = c("control", "treated"),
    labels = c("Control", "Treated")
)
state_plot$state <- factor(
    state_plot$state,
    levels = c("complete", "MAR", "MNAR", "insufficient")
)
status_by_feature <- setNames(
    fit$feature_status$retained,
    fit$feature_status$feature
)
state_feature_labels <- setNames(
    ifelse(
        status_by_feature[state_features],
        state_features,
        paste0(state_features, " (filtered)")
    ),
    state_features
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    state_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(x = condition, y = feature, fill = state)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = state),
        size = 3.3,
        colour = "#222222"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = state_feature_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            complete = "#D9EAF7",
            MAR = "#DDECCB",
            MNAR = "#FBE3C3",
            insufficient = "#F2C9C9"
        ),
        drop = FALSE,
        name = "State"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Synthetic protein") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom"
    )
```

`mixed_mechanism` is MNAR in control and MAR in treated, so routing differs by
condition. For `high_tail_mar`, control values 8, 9, and 25 give a mean of 14
and three observations from four samples. The strong observation moves the
block to MAR, illustrating the arithmetic-mean rule.

`sparse_high` exceeds the cutoff but has only one control observation, making
it `insufficient`. `all_mnar` is dropped because neither condition is complete
or MAR-like. `complete_low` stays complete: cutoffs apply only to incomplete
blocks.

# What pooling conditions would lose

Apply the same cutoff and majority rule to `condition_on_off` pooled across
samples, using original values before rescue.

```{r pooled-comparison}
pooled_values <- unname(x["condition_on_off", ])
pooled_observed <- sum(!is.na(pooled_values))
pooled_mean <- mean(pooled_values, na.rm = TRUE)
pooled_state <- if (all(!is.na(pooled_values))) {
    "complete"
} else if (pooled_mean < 12) {
    "MNAR"
} else if (pooled_observed > length(pooled_values) / 2) {
    "MAR"
} else {
    "insufficient"
}

on_off_states <- fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$feature == "condition_on_off",
    c("condition", "observed_count", "sample_count", "mean_intensity", "state")
]
on_off_states <- on_off_states[
    match(unique(condition), on_off_states$condition),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
pooled_comparison <- rbind(
    data.frame(
        scope = "Pooled original samples",
        observed_count = pooled_observed,
        sample_count = length(pooled_values),
        mean_intensity = pooled_mean,
        state = pooled_state
    ),
    data.frame(
        scope = paste(on_off_states$condition, "condition"),
        observed_count = on_off_states$observed_count,
        sample_count = on_off_states$sample_count,
        mean_intensity = on_off_states$mean_intensity,
        state = on_off_states$state
    )
)
knitr::kable(
    pooled_comparison,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Scope", "Observed", "Samples", "Mean intensity", "State")
)

on_off_status <- fit$feature_status[
    fit$feature_status$feature == "condition_on_off",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
stopifnot(
    identical(pooled_state, "insufficient"),
    identical(
        on_off_states$state[
            match(c("control", "treated"), on_off_states$condition)
        ],
        c("MNAR", "complete")
    ),
    isTRUE(on_off_status$retained)
)
```

Pooling gives four observations from eight samples and a mean above the cutoff.
Without a strict majority, the feature becomes `insufficient` and is dropped.
Condition-aware classification retains it as `MNAR` in control and `complete`
in treated.

# Why downstream imputation remains condition-specific

The separate downstream branches must also use donors from the appropriate
condition. `differential_mar` has one missing value per group and observed means
of 15 in control and 21 in treated. Mean replacement illustrates how pooling
changes that difference.

```{r condition-specific-imputation}
differential_values <- unname(x["differential_mar", ])
condition_means <- vapply(
    c("control", "treated"),
    function(condition_name) {
        mean(
            differential_values[condition == condition_name],
            na.rm = TRUE
        )
    },
    numeric(1L)
)
pooled_replacement <- mean(differential_values, na.rm = TRUE)

within_condition_values <- differential_values
for (condition_name in names(condition_means)) {
    replace_index <- condition == condition_name &
        is.na(within_condition_values)
    within_condition_values[replace_index] <-
        condition_means[[condition_name]]
}
pooled_values <- differential_values
pooled_values[is.na(pooled_values)] <- pooled_replacement

imputation_comparison <- data.frame(
    strategy = c("Within-condition stand-in", "Pooled stand-in"),
    control_replacement = c(condition_means[["control"]], pooled_replacement),
    treated_replacement = c(condition_means[["treated"]], pooled_replacement),
    control_mean = c(
        mean(within_condition_values[condition == "control"]),
        mean(pooled_values[condition == "control"])
    ),
    treated_mean = c(
        mean(within_condition_values[condition == "treated"]),
        mean(pooled_values[condition == "treated"])
    ),
    difference = c(
        mean(within_condition_values[condition == "treated"]) -
            mean(within_condition_values[condition == "control"]),
        mean(pooled_values[condition == "treated"]) -
            mean(pooled_values[condition == "control"])
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    imputation_comparison,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
        "Strategy",
        "Control replacement",
        "Treated replacement",
        "Control mean",
        "Treated mean",
        "Treated - control"
    )
)

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    imputation_comparison$difference,
    c(6, 4.5),
    tolerance = 1e-12
)))
```

```{r condition-imputation-audit, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=imputation_audit_caption}
imputation_audit_values <- rbind(
    Observed = differential_values,
    `Within-condition stand-in` = within_condition_values,
    `Pooled stand-in` = pooled_values
)
colnames(imputation_audit_values) <- colnames(x)
imputation_inserted <- rbind(rep(FALSE, ncol(x)),
    is.na(differential_values), is.na(differential_values))
imputation_audit <- data.frame(
    strategy = factor(rep(rownames(imputation_audit_values), ncol(x)),
        levels = rev(rownames(imputation_audit_values))),
    sample = factor(rep(colnames(x), each = 3L), levels = colnames(x)),
    condition = factor(rep(condition, each = 3L),
        levels = c("control", "treated"), labels = c("Control", "Treated")),
    intensity = as.vector(imputation_audit_values),
    inserted = as.vector(imputation_inserted)
)
imputation_audit_gaps <- c(
    condition_means[["treated"]] - condition_means[["control"]],
    imputation_comparison$difference
)
imputation_audit_labels <- setNames(paste0(
    rownames(imputation_audit_values), "\nDifference = ", imputation_audit_gaps
), rownames(imputation_audit_values))
ggplot2::ggplot(imputation_audit,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = strategy, fill = intensity)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(data = imputation_audit[imputation_audit$inserted, ],
        fill = NA, colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1.2, width = 0.94, height = 0.88) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = imputation_audit[!is.na(imputation_audit$intensity), ],
        ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", intensity), colour = intensity > 18),
        size = 3.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = imputation_audit[is.na(imputation_audit$intensity), ],
        shape = 4, size = 2.4, colour = "#555555") +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(cols = ggplot2::vars(condition), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = heatmap_sample_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = imputation_audit_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "white"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C",
        na.value = "#E0E0E0", limits = range(imputation_audit_values, na.rm = TRUE),
        name = "log2-like intensity") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Sample", y = NULL, title = "Inspect what each stand-in inserts") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#F2F2F2", colour = NA),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))

stopifnot(sum(imputation_inserted) == 4L)
for (strategy in seq_len(nrow(imputation_audit_values))) {
    observed <- !is.na(differential_values)
    stopifnot(identical(unname(imputation_audit_values[strategy, observed]),
        differential_values[observed]))
}
```

Within-condition replacement preserves the six-unit mean difference. Pooling
inserts 18 into both groups, shrinking the difference to 4.5. These stand-ins
illustrate donor-pool effects, not recommended MAR imputation. Cross-group
borrowing can also affect methods such as k-nearest neighbours. Impute each
routed block within its condition, then restore sample order.

# Real-data case study: Tau phosphosites in human brain

A study by
[Wesseling et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.10.029)
mapped Tau post-translational modifications in post-mortem human control and
Alzheimer's disease tissue. The underlying mass-spectrometry data are available
under PRIDE accession
[PXD020717](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD020717).

The bundled extract contains seven sites from three control and three
Alzheimer's disease soluble BA46 samples. Values reproduce MaxQuant `Intensity`
columns in `Phospho (STY)Sites.txt`; site numbers follow P10636-8, 2N4R Tau.
Source zeros become `NA`. Positive intensities are log2-transformed and rounded
to three decimals, without between-sample normalisation.

Samples, sites, and manual cutoffs of 24.5 were selected to demonstrate
classification, not estimate disease effects. The cutoffs are not from the
source study. A range-request builder under `data-raw/` regenerates the fixture
from the public MaxQuant archive.

```{r pxd020717-data}
tau_path <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "PXD020717_tau_phosphosites.csv",
    package = "imputefinder"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(tau_path))
tau_samples <- utils::read.csv(
    tau_path,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    na.strings = ""
)
tau_features <- grep("^MAPT_", names(tau_samples), value = TRUE)
tau_x <- t(as.matrix(tau_samples[, tau_features, drop = FALSE]))
colnames(tau_x) <- tau_samples$sample
storage.mode(tau_x) <- "double"
tau_condition <- tau_samples$condition

tau_fit <- classify_missingness(
    tau_x,
    group = tau_condition,
    cutoffs = c(control = 24.5, AD = 24.5),
    seed = 1L
)
tau_fit
```

The extract includes incomplete blocks on both sides of the cutoff, complete
blocks, a globally absent site, and a site without a strict observed majority.

Pooled pT217 has three observations from six samples and a below-cutoff mean,
so it receives one MNAR-like label. Condition-aware classification retains the
site as MNAR-like in control and complete in Alzheimer's disease. This
demonstrates routing, not a known missingness mechanism or a population
difference.

# Result components

- `data` - retained rows in the input representation, with any rescue values.
- `classifications` - processed statistics, original counts and means, states,
    and retention decisions by feature and condition.
- `groups` - retained `MNAR`, `MAR`, `complete`, `MAR_or_complete`, and `absent` feature
    names for each condition.
- `feature_status` - one retention decision for every original feature.
- `cutoffs`, `cutoff_diagnostics` - condition boundaries, how they were chosen,
    method details, and warnings.
- `profiles` - feature statistics, the density grid, and smoothing details.
- `seed_log` - every rescue value, including those on features later dropped.
- `groups_by_sample` - aligned condition label for every output sample.
- `call` - the matched call.
- `policies` - the resolved rescue and ambiguity choices.

## Preserve absence without rescue

No-rescue mode keeps unobserved blocks absent rather than inserting values to
enable classification.

```{r no-rescue-policy}
absence_example <- rbind(
    on_off = c(NA, NA, NA, 15, 16, 17),
    mar = c(15, NA, 16, 15, 16, 17),
    low = c(8, NA, NA, 15, 16, 17)
)
colnames(absence_example) <- paste0("s", seq_len(ncol(absence_example)))
absence_fit <- classify_missingness(
    absence_example,
    rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3),
    cutoffs = c(A = 12),
    rescue = "none"
)
knitr::kable(absence_fit$classifications[, c(
    "feature", "condition", "state", "original_observed_count",
    "original_missing_count", "original_mean_intensity"
)])
stopifnot(identical(absence_fit$data, absence_example))
absence_fit$groups$A$absent
absence_fit$profiles$A$metadata[c(
    "estimated_feature_count", "excluded_absent_feature_count"
)]
```

Absent blocks remain outside MAR and MNAR groups and need separate downstream
treatment. Unobserved conditions need no cutoff and receive an empty labelled
plot. Globally missing features are dropped. Absence does not prove a
biological on/off mechanism.

Minimum rescue can make a one-sample block `complete` without original
observations. Printing flags these blocks; `summary(fit)$seeded_complete`
counts them. Inspect `original_observed_count` and the seed log to distinguish
synthetic completeness from measured support.

# The stored missingness profile

ImputeFinder estimates incomplete and complete feature-mean densities on a
shared intensity grid for each condition. With count-weighted densities
`n_1 f_1(x)` for incomplete blocks and `n_0 f_0(x)` for complete blocks, the
profile is

```text
                n_1 f_1(x)
p_missing(x) = -------------------------
                n_1 f_1(x) + n_0 f_0(x)
```

This estimates the local proportion of incomplete blocks, not the fraction of
missing samples. Results store feature statistics, the grid, bandwidth, class
counts, warnings, and cutoff details; plotting reuses them.

```{r stored-profile}
fit$profiles$control$metadata[c("class_counts", "bandwidth", "kernel")]
head(
    fit$profiles$control$grid[
        , c("intensity", "missing_proportion", "supported")
    ]
)
```

```{r manual-profile, fig.cap=manual_profile_caption}
plot_missingness(fit, "control")
```

This nine-feature panel illustrates the stored profile, manual cutoff, and
rescue value. It is too small for automatic selection or scientific
interpretation of the transition.

# Cutoff sensitivity with known states

This experiment varies manual cutoffs from 8 to 14 for known MAR and MNAR
blocks with overlapping intensities. Complete blocks are included in the data
but excluded from classification metrics because they need no cutoff.

```{r cutoff-benchmark-data, include=FALSE}
make_benchmark_block <- function(
    means,
    observed_count,
    sample_count = 6L
) {
    block <- matrix(
        NA_real_,
        nrow = length(means),
        ncol = sample_count
    )
    offsets <- seq(-0.15, 0.15, length.out = observed_count)

    for (feature_index in seq_along(means)) {
        observed <- (
            feature_index - 1L + seq_len(observed_count) - 1L
        ) %% sample_count + 1L
        block[feature_index, observed] <-
            means[[feature_index]] + offsets
    }
    block
}

features_per_state <- 120L
benchmark_mnar <- make_benchmark_block(
    seq(8.5, 12.4, length.out = features_per_state),
    observed_count = 2L
)
benchmark_mar <- make_benchmark_block(
    seq(11.6, 15.5, length.out = features_per_state),
    observed_count = 4L
)
benchmark_complete <- make_benchmark_block(
    seq(9, 16, length.out = 60L),
    observed_count = 6L
)
cutoff_benchmark_x <- rbind(
    benchmark_mnar,
    benchmark_mar,
    benchmark_complete
)
rownames(cutoff_benchmark_x) <- c(
    sprintf("mnar_%03d", seq_len(nrow(benchmark_mnar))),
    sprintf("mar_%03d", seq_len(nrow(benchmark_mar))),
    sprintf("complete_%03d", seq_len(nrow(benchmark_complete)))
)
colnames(cutoff_benchmark_x) <- paste0(
    "benchmark_sample_",
    seq_len(ncol(cutoff_benchmark_x))
)
cutoff_benchmark_truth <- setNames(
    c(
        rep("MNAR", nrow(benchmark_mnar)),
        rep("MAR", nrow(benchmark_mar)),
        rep("complete", nrow(benchmark_complete))
    ),
    rownames(cutoff_benchmark_x)
)

cutoff_benchmark_fits <- lapply(8:14, function(cutoff) {
    classify_missingness(
        cutoff_benchmark_x,
        group = rep("benchmark", ncol(cutoff_benchmark_x)),
        cutoffs = c(benchmark = cutoff),
        seed = 1L
    )
})
names(cutoff_benchmark_fits) <- as.character(8:14)
cutoff_benchmark_metrics <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(8:14, function(cutoff) {
        benchmark_fit <- cutoff_benchmark_fits[[as.character(cutoff)]]
        prediction <- setNames(
            as.character(benchmark_fit$classifications$state),
            benchmark_fit$classifications$feature
        )
        prediction <- prediction[names(cutoff_benchmark_truth)]
        mnar_recall <- mean(
            prediction[cutoff_benchmark_truth == "MNAR"] == "MNAR"
        )
        mar_recall <- mean(
            prediction[cutoff_benchmark_truth == "MAR"] == "MAR"
        )

        data.frame(
            cutoff = cutoff,
            metric = c(
                "MNAR recall",
                "MAR recall",
                "Balanced accuracy"
            ),
            value = c(
                mnar_recall,
                mar_recall,
                mean(c(mnar_recall, mar_recall))
            ),
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    })
)
cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric <- factor(
    cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric,
    levels = c("MNAR recall", "MAR recall", "Balanced accuracy")
)
balanced_accuracy <- cutoff_benchmark_metrics[
    cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric == "Balanced accuracy",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
stopifnot(identical(
    balanced_accuracy$cutoff[which.max(balanced_accuracy$value)],
    12L
))
```

```{r cutoff-benchmark-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=cutoff_benchmark_caption}
ggplot2::ggplot(
    cutoff_benchmark_metrics,
    ggplot2::aes(x = cutoff, y = value)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = 12,
        linetype = 2,
        colour = "#555555"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#2C7FB8") +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.3, colour = "#2C7FB8") +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(metric), nrow = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 8:14) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, 1),
        breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
        labels = function(value) paste0(round(value * 100), "%")
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Manual cutoff", y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
    )
```

Lower cutoffs favour MAR recall and higher cutoffs favour MNAR recall. Balanced
accuracy peaks at the design boundary, but overlapping distributions prevent
perfect separation. This classification benchmark establishes neither a
universal cutoff nor downstream imputation or differential-analysis performance.

```{r cutoff-confusion-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.5, fig.cap=confusion_caption}
confusion_truth <- cutoff_benchmark_truth[cutoff_benchmark_truth != "complete"]
confusion_states <- c("MNAR", "MAR", "insufficient")
cutoff_confusion <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(10L, 12L, 14L), function(cutoff) {
    classifications <- cutoff_benchmark_fits[[as.character(cutoff)]]$classifications
    predicted <- setNames(as.character(classifications$state), classifications$feature)
    predicted <- predicted[names(confusion_truth)]
    stopifnot(!anyNA(predicted), all(predicted %in% confusion_states))
    counts <- table(
        truth = factor(confusion_truth, levels = c("MNAR", "MAR")),
        predicted = factor(predicted, levels = confusion_states)
    )
    recalls <- cutoff_benchmark_metrics[
        cutoff_benchmark_metrics$cutoff == cutoff &
            cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric != "Balanced accuracy", "value"
    ]
    stopifnot(
        all(rowSums(counts) == features_per_state),
        isTRUE(all.equal(
            unname(c(counts["MNAR", "MNAR"], counts["MAR", "MAR"])) /
                features_per_state,
            recalls, tolerance = 1e-12
        )),
        !any(classifications$retained[classifications$state %in% c("MNAR", "insufficient")])
    )
    cells <- as.data.frame(counts, responseName = "count")
    cells$fraction <- cells$count / features_per_state
    cells$cutoff <- paste("Cutoff", cutoff)
    cells
}))
cutoff_confusion$truth <- factor(cutoff_confusion$truth, levels = c("MAR", "MNAR"))
ggplot2::ggplot(cutoff_confusion,
    ggplot2::aes(x = predicted, y = truth, fill = fraction)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%d\n(%.1f%%)", count, 100 * fraction),
            colour = fraction > 0.55), size = 3.1
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(cutoff), nrow = 1L) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = c(MNAR = "MNAR", MAR = "MAR",
        insufficient = "Insufficient")) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "white"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C",
        limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("0%", "50%", "100%"),
        name = "Within-truth fraction") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Classifier label before filtering", y = "Known design state") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#F2F2F2", colour = NA),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))

stopifnot(sum(cutoff_confusion$count) == 3L * length(confusion_truth))
```

Low cutoffs can label sparse MNAR-designed blocks `insufficient`; high cutoffs
can label MAR-designed blocks `MNAR`. The heatmaps show pre-filter labels.
The all-MNAR rule subsequently drops every MNAR-labelled feature in this
one-condition benchmark, so state recall does not measure retention.

# Automatic cutoffs

Use manual cutoffs when domain knowledge or an analysis plan fixes the
boundary. With the default `cutoffs = NULL`, ImputeFinder finds the lower,
right-hand boundary of the lowest credible downward transition. Conditions
without partially observed blocks need no cutoff. A partial named vector uses
automatic selection for omitted conditions.

The fixed synthetic matrix below produces two clear, distinct transitions.

```{r automatic-data}
make_condition <- function(n, left, right, score_offset = 0L) {
    index <- seq_len(n)
    means <- qnorm((index - 0.5) / n, mean = 12.5, sd = 2.4)
    score <- (((index + score_offset) * 104729) %% 1000003) / 1000003
    ramp <- pmin(pmax((right - means) / (right - left), 0), 1)
    missing_probability <- 1 - (1 - 0.05) * (1 - 0.68 * ramp)
    missing <- score < missing_probability

    block <- matrix(rep(means, 4L), nrow = n)
    block[cbind(which(missing), rep(4L, sum(missing)))] <- NA_real_
    block
}

feature_count <- 200L
automatic_x <- cbind(
    make_condition(feature_count, left = 10.2, right = 11),
    make_condition(feature_count, left = 13.2, right = 14, score_offset = 37L)
)
rownames(automatic_x) <- sprintf("protein_%04d", seq_len(feature_count))
colnames(automatic_x) <- paste0("automatic_sample_", seq_len(ncol(automatic_x)))
automatic_condition <- rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 4)
```

```{r automatic-fit}
automatic_fit <- classify_missingness(
    automatic_x,
    group = automatic_condition
)
round(automatic_fit$cutoffs, 3)
vapply(
    automatic_fit$cutoff_diagnostics,
    function(diagnostic) diagnostic$source,
    character(1)
)
automatic_fit$cutoff_diagnostics$control$method
```

```{r automatic-profile, fig.cap=automatic_profile_caption}
plot_missingness(automatic_fit, "control")
```

Automatic selection needs enough complete and incomplete features, intensity
support, a decreasing missingness trend, and a credible downward transition.
When several qualify, `ambiguity = "warn"` selects the lowest and signals a
warning, retained in `cutoff_diagnostics` and the caption. Use `"error"` to
require a manual cutoff or `"lowest"` to accept the selection with stored
diagnostics only.

`quality$candidate_transitions` records alternatives, not confidence intervals
or calibrated probabilities. They do not establish a unique biological
boundary. Unsupported profiles, including flat, sparse, or missing-only
profiles, raise `imputefinder_cutoff_error` with the condition, profile, and
diagnostic. Inspect that evidence and supply a named manual cutoff.
Complete-only and absent-only conditions need none.

# Filtered data and downstream branches

`fit$data` holds retained features and their rescue anchors; `seed_log` also
covers rescues on dropped features. `fit$groups` separates retained rows by
condition into `MNAR`, `MAR`, `complete`, `absent`, and `MAR_or_complete`.
These examples use minimum rescue. Without rescue, handle `absent` rows
separately from both imputation branches.

The intended order is:

1. classify the unnormalised log2 matrix;
2. normalise the entire returned `fit$data` object with the method chosen for
    the experiment;
3. split samples by `fit$groups_by_sample`;
4. within each condition, apply an MNAR method only to its `MNAR` rows and a
    MAR method only to its `MAR_or_complete` rows;
5. recombine conditions in original sample order.

This code demonstrates splitting only. Normalisation and imputation remain
analysis-specific choices, not ImputeFinder dependencies.

```{r downstream-branches}
split_condition <- function(result, condition_name) {
    samples <- names(result$groups_by_sample)[
        result$groups_by_sample == condition_name
    ]
    condition_data <- result$data[, samples, drop = FALSE]

    list(
        MNAR = condition_data[
            result$groups[[condition_name]]$MNAR,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ],
        MAR_or_complete = condition_data[
            result$groups[[condition_name]]$MAR_or_complete,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ]
    )
}

downstream <- lapply(names(fit$groups), function(condition_name) {
    split_condition(fit, condition_name)
})
names(downstream) <- names(fit$groups)

vapply(downstream, function(branch) nrow(branch$MNAR), integer(1))
vapply(downstream, function(branch) nrow(branch$MAR_or_complete), integer(1))
c(
    on_off_in_control_MNAR =
        "condition_on_off" %in% rownames(downstream$control$MNAR),
    on_off_in_treated_MAR_or_complete =
        "condition_on_off" %in%
            rownames(downstream$treated$MAR_or_complete),
    mixed_in_control_MNAR =
        "mixed_mechanism" %in% rownames(downstream$control$MNAR),
    mixed_in_treated_MAR_or_complete =
        "mixed_mechanism" %in%
            rownames(downstream$treated$MAR_or_complete)
)
```

## Cell-level replacement masks

Use `missingness_mask()` to select only remaining missing cells within each
state. Observed and rescue values stay outside the masks:

```{r missingness-masks}
mnar_mask <- missingness_mask(fit, "MNAR")
mar_mask <- missingness_mask(fit, "MAR")
absent_mask <- missingness_mask(fit, "absent")
stopifnot(
    identical(mnar_mask | mar_mask | absent_mask, is.na(fit$data)),
    !any(mnar_mask & mar_mask),
    !any((mnar_mask | mar_mask | absent_mask)[!is.na(fit$data)])
)
colSums(mnar_mask)
colSums(mar_mask)
```

Create masks before downstream processing. Align replacement matrices to the
same feature and sample names before assigning selected cells. Masks identify
targets, not the full training data needed by an imputation method. Handle
absent blocks separately; this label does not assign a missingness mechanism.

## An illustrative routing manifest

The classification table can record a plan that routes low-intensity blocks to
MNAR methods and supported incomplete blocks to MAR methods. Complete blocks
need no replacement; the algorithms remain external.

```{r routing-manifest}
manifest_features <- c(
    "condition_on_off",
    "differential_mar",
    "mixed_mechanism"
)
routing_manifest <- fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$retained &
        fit$classifications$feature %in% manifest_features,
    c("feature", "condition", "observed_count", "missing_count", "state")
]
routing_manifest <- routing_manifest[
    order(
        match(routing_manifest$feature, manifest_features),
        match(routing_manifest$condition, unique(condition))
    ),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
rownames(routing_manifest) <- NULL

pipeline_actions <- c(
    MNAR = "send to the MNAR branch",
    MAR = "send to the MAR branch",
    complete = "carry forward unchanged"
)
routing_manifest$pipeline_action <- unname(
    pipeline_actions[as.character(routing_manifest$state)]
)
knitr::kable(
    routing_manifest,
    col.names = c("Feature", "Condition", "Observed", "Missing", "State", "Action")
)
```

```{r routing-manifest-check, include=FALSE}
on_off_route <- routing_manifest[
    routing_manifest$feature == "condition_on_off",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
stopifnot(
    identical(as.character(on_off_route$state), c("MNAR", "complete")),
    identical(
        on_off_route$pipeline_action,
        c("send to the MNAR branch", "carry forward unchanged")
    )
)
```

The manifest sends `condition_on_off` and `mixed_mechanism` to the MNAR branch
only for control samples. The treated `condition_on_off` block passes through
unchanged, while treated `mixed_mechanism` enters the MAR branch.
`differential_mar` enters the MAR branch in both conditions.

After recombination, `condition_on_off` remains available for condition
comparisons; the pooled classifier would have dropped it. The manifest records
destinations, and `fit$classifications` stores supporting evidence. Grouping
complete and MAR rows provides one non-MNAR branch without erasing their
distinct states.

# `SummarizedExperiment` input

For `SummarizedExperiment` input, select the condition column and name the assay
when more than one exists. Returned `data` preserves the representation,
metadata, unselected assay values, and sample order for retained rows. Rescue
changes only the selected assay.

```{r summarized-experiment}
se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(log2_intensity = x),
    colData = data.frame(
        condition = condition,
        row.names = colnames(x)
    )
)
fit_se <- classify_missingness(
    se,
    group_col = "condition",
    assay = "log2_intensity",
    cutoffs = c(control = 12, treated = 12)
)
identical(
    SummarizedExperiment::assay(fit_se$data, "log2_intensity"),
    fit$data
)
stopifnot(identical(missingness_mask(fit_se), missingness_mask(fit)))
```

The result records `assay_index`, so the mask uses the classified assay without
repeating its name. Keep the result's assay order unchanged.

# Comparison with state-of-the-art methods {#state-of-the-art-comparison}

ImputeFinder classifies missingness rather than estimating missing values.
Comparators include mixed imputation, matrix reconstruction, and inference
without imputation; their outputs and evaluation targets differ.

## Classification, imputation, and inference

| Method or workflow | Missingness treatment and output | Comparison with ImputeFinder |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **ImputeFinder** | Condition-specific intensity cutoffs, a majority rule, and logged rescue anchors produce states and filtered data. | Makes routing and exclusions explicit. It does not estimate all missing intensities, assign mechanism probabilities, or test differential abundance. |
| [**DEP / MSnbase mixed imputation**][dep-missing] | Applies MAR and MNAR imputers to specified subsets. DEP documents condition-aware row selection and sample-subset imputation. | Existing workflows already handle condition information. ImputeFinder supplies a feature-by-condition state table, cutoff evidence, rescue log, and drop reasons instead of the imputation itself. |
| [**QRILC and MinProb**][dep-guide] | QRILC estimates a left-censored distribution by quantile regression; MinProb draws low-intensity replacements. | Potential MNAR-branch comparators when left censoring is plausible. They replace values rather than decide which feature-condition blocks belong in that branch. |
| [**msImpute**][msimpute-paper] | Combines low-rank MAR reconstruction with an MNAR distribution using entropy-based evidence about group missingness. | Integrates missingness awareness with imputation. Its group-aware barycentric mixture differs from ImputeFinder's hard, condition-specific routing decisions. |
| [**PIMMS (2024)**][pimms-paper] | Self-supervised collaborative filtering and autoencoders learn structure to reconstruct missing intensities. | Reconstructs values rather than assigning ImputeFinder states. Learned relationships replace explicit intensity-cutoff routing. |
| [**msBayesImpute (2026)**][msbayes-paper] | Bayesian matrix factorization with a probabilistic dropout model reconstructs mixed MAR/MNAR data without predefined experimental groups. | Jointly models abundance and missingness instead of routing each condition through a hard cutoff. It requires model fitting rather than just classification. |
| [**proDA**][proda-guide] | Fits probabilistic dropout curves and moderated linear models to test differential abundance without imputing missing values. | An alternative to an imputation pipeline, not a downstream imputer. It models missingness uncertainty directly rather than producing ImputeFinder's routing states. |

Condition awareness is not unique to ImputeFinder. DEP demonstrates mixed
imputation for condition-specific absence and separate sample subsets
([DEP workflow][dep-missing]). The [`msImpute` workflow][msimpute-guide] supplies
groups for MNAR-aware imputation. A condition-blind baseline cannot represent
either method fairly.

ImputeFinder records one state per feature-condition block, allowing
`mixed_mechanism` to enter different branches across conditions. This differs
from one row-wide label but does not imply other workflows cannot express such
subsets. The on/off example tests these rules, not competing packages.

## Choosing an analysis route

Use ImputeFinder for inspectable decisions before separate downstream branches.
Validate cutoffs, exclusions, and rescue anchors alongside normalisation and
imputation. Automatic selection does not establish missingness mechanisms.

For a completed matrix, msImpute, PIMMS, and msBayesImpute offer reconstruction
with different assumptions about groups, latent structure, and dropout
([msImpute][msimpute-paper]; [PIMMS][pimms-paper];
[msBayesImpute][msbayes-paper]). These alternatives need not receive
ImputeFinder's filtered, seed-modified matrix. Splitting can remove information
that joint models use.

For differential abundance without imputation, consider proDA's dropout model
([documentation][proda-guide]). Start from original data that preserve
missingness, with suitable preprocessing, rather than treating rescue anchors
as observations. This is separate from the normalise-then-impute workflow.

## What the evidence does and does not establish

The cited reconstruction studies evaluate their own methods and datasets, not
ImputeFinder. They establish no universal winner across acquisition modes or
sample sizes. msBayesImpute reports limitations for very small studies despite
favorable benchmark results
([msBayesImpute][msbayes-paper]).

This vignette compares methods conceptually, not through a head-to-head
benchmark. The cutoff sweep measures simulated-state recovery; mean stand-ins
demonstrate donor-pool effects without running the cited imputers. Unknown
missing values in the Tau extract prevent assessment of imputation accuracy or
true missingness mechanisms.

A fair study compares complete analysis routes on shared data and prespecified
endpoints. Include random and abundance-dependent masking, independent spike-in
or dilution data, and condition-specific absence. Measure reconstruction error
at held-out values, stratified by abundance and missingness design. For
differential abundance, assess effect bias, sensitivity, and empirical false
discovery rate against known contrasts. Report retention so filtering cannot
hide difficult cases. Record versions, preprocessing, tuning, seeds, runtime,
and memory. Keep evaluation truth out of tuning; classification accuracy alone
does not establish valid inference.

[dep-missing]: https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.22/bioc/vignettes/DEP/inst/doc/MissingValues.html
[dep-guide]: https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.22/bioc/vignettes/DEP/inst/doc/DEP.html
[msimpute-paper]: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mcpro.2023.100558
[msimpute-guide]: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/msImpute/inst/doc/msImpute-vignette.html
[pimms-paper]: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-48711-5
[msbayes-paper]: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-026-02106-3
[proda-guide]: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/proDA/inst/doc/Introduction.html

# Limitations

- The cutoff is a model assumption. Biology, acquisition, and preprocessing can
    produce patterns without one descending intensity transition.
- Automatic breakpoint selection needs both incomplete and complete features.
    When the data do not support a clear transition, use a manual cutoff.
- Arithmetic means are sensitive to strong observations by design.
- Rescue anchors are artificial values. Preserve `seed_log` with the analysis
    and assess their influence downstream. Select `rescue = "none"` to preserve
    missing cells instead. Neither policy establishes a missingness mechanism.
- Classification is heuristic. ImputeFinder does not prove mechanisms, choose
    an imputation algorithm, or validate the final biological analysis.

Tests cover intensity-independent MAR, intensity-dependent MNAR, on/off
features, group sizes, cutoffs, rescue seeds, and name permutations. They do not
establish performance for arbitrary proteomics experiments.
